en.headline: Flower Market hosts mini sports day and launches ticket-stub discounts with Mong Kok…
en.dek: More than 50 shops joined the pilot scheme offering up to 25 per cent off with specified Hong Kong Premier League match stubs, while free activity booths ran outside the stadium on Monday.
body: The Flower Market in Mong Kok held a mini sports day on Monday and launched a pilot ticket-stub discount scheme linking the district with nearby Mong Kok Stadium, according to organisers.

The event, jointly organised by the Blue Sky Development Community Development Association and the Urban Renewal Authority, included free activity zones where residents could try drone football and other sports. Secretary for Culture, Sports and Tourism Rosanna Law attended the launch and visited participating shops, purchasing flowers and flower tea.

From Monday until the end of the year, holders of ticket stubs from five specified Hong Kong Premier League matches at Mong Kok Stadium can enjoy discounts of up to 25 per cent at more than 50 Flower Market shops on dining and shopping. The Urban Renewal Authority said the scheme is a new attempt to encourage spectators to explore the market’s character and help merchants diversify their business.
Organisers noted that more than 50 shops had joined by Monday afternoon. The first match under the scheme was the Lee Man versus Kitchee fixture later on Monday.

zh.headline: 花墟舉辦細運會並推出與旺角大球場票尾優惠試點
zh.dek: 超過五十間商戶參與試點，憑指定港超聯賽事票尾可享低至七五折，周一在球場外設免費運動體驗攤位。
body: 旺角花墟周一舉辦「花墟細運會」，並推出與附近旺角大球場連結的票尾優惠試點，據主辦單位。
活動由青途發展社區發展協會與市區重建局合辦，設有簡易運動體驗區，市民可免費試玩無人機足球等項目。文化體育及旅遊局局長羅淑佩出席啟動禮，並到訪參與商戶購買鮮花及花茶。
由周一起至年底，市民憑旺角大球場五場指定港超聯賽事門票票尾，可在花墟超過五十間商戶享有購物及餐飲優惠，折扣最低至七五折。市建局指，這是新嘗試，鼓勵市民看波之餘感受花墟特色，亦幫助商戶拓展經營模式。
主辦單位表示，截至周一下午已有五十多間店舖參與。是日首場賽事為理文對傑志的港超聯。
